$ hemma add service --help
exit: 0
--- stdout ---
--- stderr ---
hemma add service — declare a service and generate its DNS/Caddy config

Usage: hemma add service <name> --fqdn <fqdn> --host <host> --backend <name:port> [--auth-mode forward|oidc|external] [--auth-groups <g1,g2>] [--bypass-paths <p1,p2>] [--auth-policy-local <p>] [--auth-policy-public <p>] [--tunnel]

With no flags (and stdin a terminal) an interactive editor opens instead: the
fqdn is pre-filled with <name>.<domain> when exactly one domain is defined and
validated live (must match a domain, must not collide with another service),
the host and auth mode are pickers, tunnel is a confirm, auth groups are a
multi-select built from the groups that actually exist — on users in the auth
provider's users database (members shown per group) and on other services —
plus a 'new group…' escape hatch, and auth bypass paths are one per line. On
submit it prints the collected fields and runs the exact same validation and
sync path as the flags form; Ctrl-C touches nothing. Non-interactive callers
must pass flags. ('disabled' is not offered when adding — a service is added to
work; turn it off later with 'hemma disable service'.)

Flags:
  -f, --fqdn <fqdn>       Public name the service is reached at (must match a declared domain).
  -H, --host <host>       Host (repo directory) that runs the service.
  -b, --backend <n:port>  reverse_proxy upstream, e.g. mealie:9000.
      --auth-mode <mode>  How the service authenticates (default none):
                            none      no authentication.
                            forward   Authelia forward-auth — imports the (auth) snippet
                                      (a gate); requires 'hemma defaults set auth-snippet <path>'.
                            oidc      Authelia, but the app speaks OIDC itself — no gate,
                                      and hemma verifies an Authelia OIDC client exists.
                            external  authenticated by something that is NOT Authelia (the
                                      app's own login, an API token, an edge proxy like
                                      Cloudflare Access). Renders like oidc — no gate — but
                                      hemma verifies nothing. Use this, NOT oidc, when
                                      Authelia is not involved.
      --auth-groups <gs>  Comma-separated auth provider group names allowed access; flows into
                          the generated access-control rules (multiple groups are OR'd).
                          Requires an auth mode (forward or oidc).
      --bypass-paths <p>  Comma-separated request paths exempted from the auth gate (e.g. a
                          Subsonic-API path that a native client can't complete a browser
                          login for). Requires an auth mode that uses hemma's provider
                          (forward or oidc); renders as Authelia 'policy: bypass' rules with
                          no subject, since Authelia forbids pairing bypass with one.
      --auth              Back-compat shorthand for --auth-mode forward.
      --auth-policy-local <p>
      --auth-policy-public <p>
                          Per-horizon auth requirement: bypass|one_factor|two_factor|deny.
                          Unset means one_factor on both horizons, which is what a bare
                          --auth-mode forward has always meant. "local" is a request whose
                          resolved client IP is in defaults.local_networks; "public" is
                          everything else. Forward or oidc mode (oidc has no bypass). Effective only when the
                          reverse proxy resolves the true client IP (see 'update host
                          --trusted-proxies') — otherwise everything is treated as public,
                          which is the safe direction.
      --tunnel            Generate a cloudflared tunnel ingress entry for this
                          service, so the internet can reach it. Omit for local-only
                          (every service is reachable on the LAN either way).
                          Accepts --public as a pre-rename alias.
                          Writes the entry into this host's cloudflared
                          config.yml (needs defaults.tunnel-dir set — otherwise the
                          entry is skipped and 'hemma doctor' flags the drift).

Regenerates files immediately, then prints which hosts need 'hemma apply'.
